# Bulk quote investigation

Contract: `README.md` says total cents equals unit cents times quantity, with no discounts. The reported symptom was an undercharge on bulk quotes; clearing the process-local cache appeared to help once.

| Run | State and change | Prediction | Observation | Implication |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Baseline | Original `quote.py`; `python -c "import quote; print('qty=9 cached:', quote.quote(100,9)); print('qty=10 cached:', quote.quote(100,10)); quote.CACHE.clear(); print('qty=10 after clear:', quote.quote(100,10)); print('qty=10 uncached:', quote.quote(100,10,False)); print('cache:', quote.CACHE)"` | A stale cache would stop undercharging after clear or when bypassed. | All four totals were `900`; the final cache was `{(100, 10): 900}`. 10 units should cost `1000`. | Cache state does not explain this reproduction. |
| Trace | Original `quote.py`; quantity `10` reaches `quantity - 1` before multiplication. | The adjustment should undercharge every fresh quote at or above 10 by one unit. | Fresh cached and uncached calls both returned `900`; quantity 9 returned `900`. | The quantity adjustment explains the boundary and cache-independent failure. |
| Fix check | Removed the quantity adjustment; checked `(100,9)`, `(100,10)`, `(100,11)`, `(275,25)` with cache both enabled and disabled, clearing it before each case. | Every result should equal unit cents times quantity. | `900`, `1000`, `1100`, and `6875` respectively in both modes; all assertions passed. | The original failure boundary and other bulk values now follow the contract. |
| CLI check | `python quote.py --qty 10` and `python quote.py --qty 10 --no-cache` | Both paths should return `1000`. | Both returned `total_cents: 1000`. | The CLI reaches the corrected behavior. |

The pre-fix command was run before editing. The fix check and CLI check were run after editing in this same Python 3 fixture. There is no separate regression test file; the baseline and post-fix command results are retained here.

# Bulk quote investigation

| Run | State/change | Observation | Implication |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Baseline | `python quote.py --qty 10` and `--no-cache` | Both returned 900 cents at 100 cents/unit (expected 1000). | Undercharge is not dependent on cache state. |

Cause: `quote()` subtracted one from every quantity >= 10, despite README contract stating there are no discounts. Cache clearing appeared helpful only coincidentally; the same wrong result is computed on a cache miss and with caching disabled.

Limitations: no pre-existing automated test suite/test seam was present; verification used focused Python assertions and CLI checks. No deployment or broader integration behavior was tested.

# Bulk quote investigation

## Experiment ledger

| Run | State and change | Prediction | Observation | Implication |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Baseline | `python quote.py --qty 10` (`unit=100`, cache enabled) | Expected 1000 cents | Returned 900 cents | Reproduced the undercharge. |
| Cache comparison | In one Python process, cleared `quote.CACHE`, then called `quote.quote(100, 10, True)` and `quote.quote(100, 10, False)` | Stale cache predicts differing results; deterministic calculation predicts the same | Both returned 900; enabled mode cached `{(100, 10): 900}` | Cache is not required for the failure; stale cache is not the supported cause. |
| CLI bypass | `python quote.py --qty 10 --no-cache` | Cache-specific cause predicts resolution | Returned 900 cents | Cache bypass does not resolve the failure. |
| User observation | Cache clearing appeared to help once (reported; no exact inputs/output available) | A cache cause would reproduce a cache-dependent difference | Not reproducible in controlled comparison above | Retained as contradictory but unverified evidence; insufficient to explain repeatable output. |

## Cause and change

`quote()` used `quantity - 1` for every quantity of 10 or more, despite the
README contract that there are no discounts and total is unit cents times
quantity. The same result with cache enabled and bypassed supports this
deterministic arithmetic defect over stale cache. The function now multiplies
unit cents by the requested quantity directly.

## Verification

After the change, `python -m unittest -v` checks quantity 10 with cache enabled
and disabled. `python quote.py --qty 10` and
`python quote.py --qty 10 --no-cache` are also rerun. The specific reported
quantity is verified; other boundary quantities and any external production
behavior are outside this fixture's evidence.
